name: Amharic
notes: Amharic Ethiopic (Ge'ez) script. Abugida where each character encodes consonant + vowel; 7 vowel orders per consonant row. Ejectives: Kʼ, Tʼ, Čʼ, Pʼ, Tsʼ are phonemic. The 6th order (ə-vowel) is the inherent vowel. Ä, ʕ (Ayin) present in traditional script but has no phonemic value distinct from /ʔ/ in Amharic (Hayward & Hayward 1992 give Amharic a single glottal series with no pharyngeal); the ዐ row is mapped to the same /ʔ/ series as the አ row rather than to a separate ʕ, its 6th-order ዕ following እ to /ɨ/ for the same reason. Stress exemption: Amharic has no phonemically contrastive word stress; prominence is weak/variable and is not marked by or predictable from the Ge'ez abugida modeled here; no stress block is declared. Source: Leslau, Reference Grammar of Amharic (1995). Labialisation. Amharic labialised consonants are phonemic, not derivable from a /Cua/ or /Coa/ vowel sequence nor from /w/-loss, and are written with dedicated Ethiopic glyphs. Ado (2020, p. 55) puts the inventory at 19: hʷ lʷ mʷ rʷ sʷ ʃʷ kʼʷ bʷ tʷ nʷ kʷ zʷ dʷ ɡʷ tʼʷ tʃʼʷ sʼʷ fʷ ʒʷ. Ado transcribes the ጸ row as sʼ, so his sʼʷ is this table's tsʼʷ (ጿ); the affricate notation follows the ጸ row already in the table and the vox_communis gold, which transcribes ተገልጿል as t ə ɡ ə l ɨ t͡sʼʷ a l. Five labialised glyphs are mapped that Ado's 19 do not name. ጇ /dʒʷa/ is supported elsewhere in the same paper (dʒʷɜro 'ear', example 8e) and ጷ /pʼʷa/ by the /pʼʷ/ of Hayward & Hayward's (1992) labialised set; ቿ /tʃʷa/, ኗ /ɲʷa/, ፗ /pʷa/ and ቯ /vʷa/ rest on row regularity alone, ፗ and ቯ extending the two rows that occur only in loanwords. Orthographic homophony. Ethiopic keeps apart in writing several rows that fell together in speech. Hayward & Hayward (1992) give Amharic a single /h/, with no pharyngeal /ħ/ and no velar /x/, and a single ejective sibilant, with no separate /tsʼ/; their consonant chart (p. 48) has no uvular column at all, so the ቅ row (traditionally called ḳā in the Ge'ez syllabary naming) is the velar ejective /kʼ/, not the uvular /q/ this table previously carried — their own example word list gives kʼəddədə 'he tore st.' (p. 49) with the velar ejective symbol. The ሀ, ሐ, ኀ and ኸ rows are therefore all mapped to /h/ (the ኸ row writes /x/ in foreign spellings), and the archaic ፀ row carries the same value as ጸ. These letters must still transcribe: an unmapped character is deleted silently and truncates the rest of the word around it. Deliberately unmapped. The Ethiopic block encodes more than the Amharic orthography uses. The ቐ, ዸ and ጘ rows and the ፘ ፙ ፚ letters write consonants absent from the Amharic consonant chart of Hayward & Hayward (1992) and belong to other languages of the script. The eighth-order 'oa' letters ሇ ቇ ኇ ኯ ጏ ፇ ዏ ዯ sit in a syllable slot Unicode reanalysed for extended Ethiopic rather than in the Amharic seven-order paradigm, and ኧ is the labialised slot of the ʾ row, which cannot be labialised in an inventory with no /ʔʷ/. None of these occurs anywhere in the 41,407 Ethiopic characters of the shipped wikipron and vox_communis gold. The Ethiopic wordspace ፡ (and ። ፣) are punctuation (Unicode category Po), already stripped generically by the tokenizer, and are left unmapped rather than given a spec entry. WikiPron gold forensics (n=388, provenance crowd-scraped, PER 0.3662, 95% bootstrap CI [0.3445, 0.3881]). Two things the abugida structurally cannot write account for most of that PER. Gemination is contrastive (Hayward & Hayward 1992, p. 49: "[a]ll consonants with the exception of /p, pʷʼ, tʷʼ, h, hʷ/ have geminate counterparts") but never marked in the script; folding length out of both hypothesis and gold drops PER to 0.3327 (CI [0.3093, 0.3552]). The 6th order (sädis) is ambiguous in the script between /ɨ/ and a bare consonant with no vowel; folding that distinction out of both sides drops PER to 0.1681 (CI [0.1520, 0.1866]) alone, 0.1048 (CI [0.0896, 0.1205]) combined with the gemination fold — 30 words needed only the gemination fold to match exactly, 119 needed only the 6th-order fold, and 59 needed both, against 42 exact matches at the raw PER. After the combined fold, 68 of the 138 remaining mismatches involved the ር row. Hayward & Hayward's Conventions section (1992, p. 50) states plainly: "Single /r/ is a tap, geminate /rr/ a trill" — an allophonic rule conditioned on gemination, not a free transcription choice. The table now emits the tap /ɾ/ for every ር row entry, since gemination is never written in Ge'ez and an unmarked ር is therefore always read as the singleton, elsewhere case. This resolves 39 of the 68 (raw PER 0.3662 -> 0.3296, combined-fold ceiling 0.1048 -> 0.0581); the remaining 29 stay unresolved because the gold word is in fact geminate (trill [r]) and gemination cannot be recovered from the spelling at all — the same structural gap the gemination fold already measures, surfacing again on this particular consonant rather than as a new defect. A further ~59 of the remaining mismatches begin with a laryngeal (ሀ/ሐ/አ, all /h/ or /ʔ/) and show the order-1 vowel realized as gold [a] rather than [ə] (e.g. ሐኪም hyp. həkimə vs. gold hakim); Hayward & Hayward's own specimen list has the same word ("hakim ‘doctor’", p. 49, itself an Arabic loan, ḥakīm) with that vowel, but their vowel-allophony discussion (p. 50) conditions only [ɪ ʊ ɛ ɔ] on postalveolar/palatal/labialised consonants and says nothing about a laryngeal trigger, so no rule is added for this: it rests on one loanword example, not a described alternation, and is documented as measured residual rather than sourced. The combined fold with the /kʼ/, /ʔ/ and /ɾ/ corrections above and no other change measures PER 0.0581 (CI [0.0468, 0.0694]); the row is input-limited, well under the 0.25 ceiling-gating threshold, and the raw PER (0.3296 with these corrections, down from the unmodified spec's 0.3662) overwhelmingly reflects what the Ge'ez abugida cannot write rather than a spec defect.

sources.author: Ado, Derib
sources.title: Revisiting the status of labialised consonants in contemporary Amharic
sources.notes: Argues the labialised consonants written with the dedicated Ethiopic ⟨wa⟩ glyphs are phonemically contrastive in Amharic rather than a /Cua/ sequence or a lost /w/, and fixes the inventory at 19 on p. 55; the agentive forms ʃʷami 'one who appoints', tʃʼʷahi 'one who shouts' and sʼʷami 'one who fasts' are its proof words, and /ʒʷ/ rests on ʒʷa 'heavy rain' and burʒʷa 'bourgeois'.

sources.notes: Consonant chart for the Addis Ababa standard: one /h/ (no pharyngeal or velar fricative), one ejective sibilant, and a labialised set including /pʼʷ/, described there together with /p/ and /pʼ/ as extremely rare and confined to words of foreign origin, and /hʷ/ (hʷala 'after', written ሗላ).

ancestors.notes: Geʽez ancestor/prestige source: liturgical and literary layer.
Cushitic (Agaw) substrate: SOV order, ejectives, gemination — the chief non-Semitic layer.
Arabic adstrate: religious and lexical borrowing.

wikipron.measured: Two things the Ge'ez abugida structurally cannot write account for most of the wikipron/am residual (raw PER 0.3662, n=388): gemination is contrastive but never marked in the script (Hayward & Hayward 1992 p.49), and the sixth order (sadis) is ambiguous between /i/ and a bare consonant with no vowel. Folding gemination out of both sides drops PER to 0.3327; folding the sixth-order ambiguity as well drops it to 0.1048; after also correcting three sourced grapheme values (kʼ for the qa row, the ʔ/ʕ merger, and the tap /ɾ/ for r-row gemination-conditioned by Hayward & Hayward p.50), the combined-fold ceiling is 0.0581 -- well under the 0.25 gating threshold -- so the row is input-limited.
